idiom_name: private member functions + local functions for one-off steps
implementation_notes: Kotlin keeps the classic shape - a public function whose body is an outline, steps as private member functions - and adds two placements that replace private methods for stateless steps: top-level functions marked `private`, which are visible only inside their file (the visibility docs: at top level `private` means file-private), and local functions declared inside the composed function, which can capture the enclosing scope and are documented precisely for hiding an implementation (the `dfs` example). Prefer a private member when the step uses instance state, a file-private top-level function when it is shared inside the file but stateless, and a local function when exactly one outline calls it - promoting it to a member the moment a second caller appears. Expression bodies (`fun isValid() = ...`) keep one-line steps reading like the outline line they replace, and `internal` is module-wide, never a synonym for private.
pitfalls: Top-level `private` is file-private, not class-private: every other declaration in the same file can call the step, so a step that must belong to one type stays a member.

A local function or lambda captures the enclosing receiver; storing it in a property or passing it to a coroutine keeps the whole object alive, so use a member function when the step must outlive the call.
Local functions cannot carry visibility modifiers and are not reachable by tests; as soon as a step needs its own contract, promote it to a member or a file-private top-level function.
